find: A grid-exact beat almost always means programming or a drum machine. Those have been common since the early 1980s, so an exact beat rules out the live-band rock of the 1960s and 1970s.
replace: A grid-exact beat can suggest programming or a drum machine, but it does not date a track on its own: drum machines appear on records from the early 1970s, and many tracks from the 1980s onwards still use a live drummer, so treat the beat as one clue to weigh alongside the production, the instruments and the vocal style.
note: F1: Drum machines were used in popular and rock recordings before the 1980s. | orchestrator: replacement extended to keep L4 above the 700-word validator floor (was 709 words).

expect: Listen to the drum timing. Human playing pushes and pulls slightly; grid-exact timing means programming or a drum machine, common since the early 1980s, so it rules out 1960s and 1970s rock.

expect:
Students may include:
• Ten-bar instrumental introduction opening with a two-bar arpeggiated piano riff in octaves.
• Ten-bar verses; an eleven-bar first bridge and an eight-bar second bridge; a guitar-led instrumental solo.
• No chorus — the melodic hook 'the seven seas of Rhye' does the chorus's job; outro quotes 'Oh! I Do Like to Be Beside the Seaside' and fades.
value: Indicative answer: A ten-bar arpeggiated piano introduction, verses and contrast sections, a guitar solo, no repeating chorus, then a seaside-song fade-out.

expect:
Students may include:
• Opens in B flat major (a cappella and ballad sections), moving towards E flat major.
• Abrupt modulation to the unrelated key of A major for the opera section.
• Hard rock section in E flat major; the song ends in F major — a different key from where it began.
value: Indicative answer: It opens in B flat major, moves through E flat major, shifts to A major in the opera section, returns to E flat major for hard rock and ends in F major.

expect:
Students may include:
• Both are fundamentally in 4/4 (simple time).
• Bohemian Rhapsody interrupts it with single bars of 5/4 and 9/8, and its rock section switches to 12/8 compound time.
• Love of My Life stays 4/4 but slips in a single 3/4 bar in each verse, a 6/4 bar before the instrumental bridge and a 2/4 bar before the solo.
• In both, the changes serve the vocal phrasing rather than a dance feel.
value: Indicative answer: Both are mainly in 4/4. Bohemian Rhapsody includes 5/4, 9/8 and 12/8; Love of My Life changes metre to follow vocal phrasing.
note: F4: Replace an unsupported credit statement with an indicative answer.

expect:
Students may include:
• Bohemian Rhapsody: through-composed chain of six contrasting sections (a cappella, ballad, solo, opera, rock, outro) with no chorus, unified by returning material and key relationships.
• Seven Seas of Rhye: compact hard rock design — riff-based introduction, verses and two bridges of irregular lengths (10/11/8 bars), instrumental solo, no chorus, quoted-song fade-out.
• Love of My Life: ballad form — piano introduction, verses with instrumental bridge and guitar solo, coda; sectional repetition with varied scoring (harp, guitar).
• Credit precise supporting detail: keys per section, bar counts, the hook standing in for a chorus.
value: Indicative answer: Bohemian Rhapsody chains six contrasting sections without a chorus; Seven Seas of Rhye uses a riff-based rock design; Love of My Life is a ballad with an introduction, verses, bridge, solo and coda.
note: F4: Replace an unsupported credit statement with an indicative answer.
